title: Port States: What Happens at the Network Level
description: Three scenarios showing what happens during a TCP SYN scan depending on the port state. The response — or absence of response — is exactly what Nmap measures to determine each port's state.

nodes.label:
Target Port
State: OPEN
nodes.detail: A service is listening — SYN/ACK returned

nodes.label:
Nmap sends RST
(tears down connection)
nodes.detail: Half-open connection immediately closed — handshake never completes

nodes.label:
Target Port
State: CLOSED
nodes.detail: Host alive, no service listening — RST returned by host

nodes.label: Firewall
nodes.detail: Configured to drop packets to this port silently

nodes.label:
Target Port
State: FILTERED
nodes.detail: State unknown — may or may not have a service

edges.label: Nmap sends RST immediately (never completes handshake)

caption:
OPEN: Your SYN reaches the target port. A service is listening and responds with SYN/ACK — connection accepted. Nmap immediately sends RST to close the half-open connection. Port confirmed open.

CLOSED: Your SYN reaches the host, but no service is listening on this port. The host itself sends RST — a definitive 'nothing here.' The host is alive and responding; this specific door is simply empty.

FILTERED: Your SYN is intercepted by a firewall before it reaches the host. No response arrives. Nmap cannot determine whether the port is open or closed — the state is unknown. Filtered is not the same as empty.
